newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pernod sees spirit mkt shrinkage in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pernod sees spirit mkt shrinkage in 1997.

text.p: Pernod-Ricard director general Thierry Jacquillat said on Wednesday that the French spirits market could fall by two to three percent in 1997 as a result of a rise in the spirits tax.
"With the new proposal (tax) we estimate the drop in the spirit market in France will be two to three percent next year," Jacquillat told an investment conference.

The French government had originally proposed as part of its 1997 budget to raise taxes on spirits by about 17 percent, but under pressure from spirits producers agreed to cut the increase to 4.97 percent.

Jacquillat said that if the 17-percent rise had gone through the company estimated the market would fall by about eight percent and lead to an earnings shortfall of some 200 million francs for Pernod-Ricard.
